samples.text:
The pie charts show how the employees of a company worked in 2019 and 2024, and the bar chart shows how much the company spent for its offices from 2019 to 2024.

In 2019 most of employees worked in the office full-time, it was 82%. Only 12% worked hybrid and 6% were fully remote. However, in 2024 the situation was very different. Office full-time decreased to 24% and hybrid became the most popular with 58%. Fully remote also increased to 18%, which is three times more than 2019.

The bar chart shows that the total office costs was $6.4 million in 2019. In 2020 it fell to $5.7 million because energy and services went down from $1.6 million to $0.9 million, but the rent stayed at $4.8 million until 2021. In 2022 the rent decreased to $3.1 million and the total was $4.4 million. In 2024 the total cost was only $3.6 million, with rent $2.6 million and energy $1.0 million.

Overall, fewer employees worked in the office full-time and the company office costs decreased a lot.
samples.why: Overview present but brief and placed at the end · all three visuals covered with accurate figures · adequate but mechanical linking · limited vocabulary · errors in prepositions, articles, agreement and a comma splice.

samples.text:
The two pie charts compare the working arrangements of a company's employees in 2019 and 2024, while the bar chart illustrates the company's yearly office costs, broken down into rent and energy and services, over the same period.

Overall, there was a major shift away from full-time office work towards hybrid working. At the same time, the company's total office costs fell considerably, mainly as a result of lower rent.

In 2019, the vast majority of staff (82%) worked in the office full-time, while only 12% had hybrid arrangements and 6% worked fully remotely. Five years later, the picture had changed dramatically: hybrid working had become the norm for 58% of employees, and the proportion working fully remotely had tripled to 18%. Only 24% were still based in office full-time.

Regarding costs, the company spent $6.4 million on its offices in 2019. Rent remained at $4.8 million for three years before dropping to $3.1 million in 2022 and $2.6 million in 2024. Spending on energy and services fluctuated, falling from $1.6 million to $0.9 million in 2020 and then recovering slightly to $1.3 million in 2022, before ending at $1.0 million. As a result, total costs fell by $2.8 million to $3.6 million.
samples.why: Clear overview linking working patterns and costs · key changes highlighted with accurate comparisons · logical progression and good linkers · some less common vocabulary (the norm, fluctuated) · one minor article slip.

samples.text:
The pie charts show how a company's workforce was divided between office-based, hybrid and fully remote working in 2019 and 2024, and the bar chart details the company's annual office costs from 2019 to 2024.

Over the five years, hybrid working replaced full-time office attendance as the predominant arrangement, and the company's office costs fell substantially, with rent accounting for most of the saving.

In 2019, 82% of employees worked full-time in the office, compared with 12% on hybrid arrangements and just 6% working fully remotely. By 2024 this pattern had been largely reversed: hybrid working accounted for 58% of staff, full-time office workers for only 24%, and the remote share had tripled to 18%.

Total office costs stood at $6.4 million in 2019. Rent was fixed at $4.8 million for the first three years, so the initial dip to $5.7 million in 2020 stemmed entirely from lower spending on energy and services, which fell from $1.6 million to $0.9 million. Rent was then cut to $3.1 million in 2022 and to $2.6 million in 2024, and energy and service costs, after a modest rebound to $1.3 million, eased back to $1.0 million. Consequently, total costs in 2024 were $3.6 million, some 44% below the 2019 figure.
samples.why: Sharp overview covering all three visuals · data interpreted skilfully (source of the 2020 dip, percentage saving) · cohesion seamless · precise vocabulary (predominant, stemmed, eased back) · error-free, varied structures.
